claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-08-25 reports: FAO relays an IPC projection that 286,000 people (23%) face IPC 3+ in Oct 2026-Mar 2027; El Nino-linked low rain and high temperatures may reduce farm labour demand and incomes.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: October 2026–March 2027 national forecast, not observed outcomes; combines climate and non-weather drivers.

gaps: Main directly checked the original government communication, IMF report, journal table of adaptation barriers, and FAO harvest/forecast distinctions. No climate-to-violence pathway is inferred.
Lubombo field data are 2025 self-reports from selected communities. Institutional/finance constraints must not be represented as insecurity blocking a named climate project.

executive_assessment.text: Shiselweni/Lubombo vulnerability and named Lubombo survey communities add spatial and social detail, with dated national and survey baselines kept distinct.

Irrigation and reported coping practices show capacity alongside finance, information and tenure barriers. The 2026 harvest estimate and 2026/27 food-security forecast have different evidential status.
